Description: Point-based (gage-level) metadata used as a station-level predictors, not derived from zonal aggregation.
Notes: Represents site location in degrees east or west. Useful for detecting climatic or physiographic gradients (moisture availability, storm type).
Effective Analytical Resolution: Point-defined (gage-level metadata)

Description: Point-based (gage-level) metadata used as a station-level predictors, not derived from zonal aggregation.
Notes: Represents site location in degrees north. Commonly used to capture latitudinal patterns in climate and hydrology (e.g., temperature, seasonality).
Effective Analytical Resolution: Point-defined (gage-level metadata)

Description: Point-based (gage-level) metadata used as a station-level predictors, not derived from zonal aggregation.
Notes: Elevation of the gage site above sea level. Influences temperature, snowpack, and runoff timing
Effective Analytical Resolution: Point-defined (gage-level metadata)

Description: Point-based (gage-level) metadata used as a station-level predictors, not derived from zonal aggregation.
Notes: Commonly used as a spatial predictor in hydrologic modeling.
Effective Analytical Resolution: Point-defined (gage-level metadata)

Description: Dominant Koppen Geiger climate class, aggregated to macroregional zones.
Notes: Provides broad-scale climate context (e.g., humid continental vs. semi-arid). Useful for regional stratification.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km (macroregional zone level)

Description: Count of unique USDA Plant Hardiness Zones, aggregated to macroregional zones.
Notes: Reflects cold hardiness diversity; transitional zones may influence vegetation, snowmelt timing, and freeze-�thaw cycles.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km (macroregional zone level)

Description: Dominant USDA Plant Hardiness Zone, aggregated to macroregional zones.
Notes: Captures dominant cold tolerance regime based on minimum winter temperatures. Relevant for snowmelt timing and freeze-thaw sensitivity.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km (macroregional zone level)

Description: Fraction of cropland (NLCD), aggregated to macroregional zones.
Notes: Indicates anthropogenic land use in agricultural regions. Associated with increased runoff, reduced infiltration, and higher ET demand.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km (macroregional zone level)

Description: Fraction of forested land (NLCD), aggregated to macroregional zones.
Notes: Forest cover enhances interception and storage. Typically reduces peak flows and lowers skew.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km (macroregional zone level)

Description: Fraction of grassland (NLCD), aggregated to macroregional zones.
Notes: Moderates evapotranspiration and infiltration rates; especially important in mixed rangeland systems.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km (macroregional zone level)

Description: Fraction of urban land (NLCD), aggregated to macroregional zones.
Notes: Urban development increases imperviousness; strongly associated with peak flow generation and positive flood skew.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km (macroregional zone level)

Description: Mean slope (from NED), aggregated to macroregional zones.
Notes: Describes average terrain steepness. Helps distinguish rugged uplands from flatter plains.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km (macroregional zone level)

Description: Median slope (from NED), aggregated to macroregional zones.
Notes: Reflects typical terrain slope. More robust to outliers than the mean; useful for evaluating runoff tendency.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km (macroregional zone level)

Description: Mean elevation of gage locations, aggregated to macroregional zones.
Notes: Represents elevational regime. Influences climate, snow duration, and runoff seasonality.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km (macroregional zone level)

Description: Zonal median of total annual precipitation from PRISM 1991 to 2020 climatological normals, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Represents typical annual moisture supply; important for soil moisture availability, runoff potential, and vegetation productivity.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level II ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Zonal median of total annual precipitation from PRISM 1991 to 2020 climatological normals, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Governs evapotranspiration, freeze thaw, and snowpack formation. Represents the baseline thermal regime.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level II ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Zonal mean of the percentage of annual precipitation falling May to August from PRISM 1991 to 2020 climatological normals, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Characterizes warm-season water input. Useful for identifying storm-driven systems tied to convective seasonality.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level II ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Zonal mean of the percentage of annual precipitation falling May to August from PRISM 1991 to 2020 climatological normals, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Captures the typical proportion of precipitation falling in the warm season, which is important for Great Plains hydrology.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level II ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Zonal median of annual NDVI amplitude for 2016 MODIS data, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Captures seasonal variation in greenness. High amplitude reflects strong vegetation response to climate fluctuations.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level II ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Zonal median of the interquartile range (IQR) of NDVI values for 2016 MODIS data, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Describes central spread of seasonal greenness. Robust to outliers and well-suited to fragmented or transitional landscapes.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level II ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Zonal median of the length of the 2016 growing season (NDVI-based), aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Indicates length of vegetative activity. Influences evapotranspiration rates and baseflow timing.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level II ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Zonal median of the seasonal peak NDVI for 2016 MODIS data, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Represents seasonal greenness maximum. Serves as a proxy for peak vegetation productivity.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level II ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Zonal mean of NED slope values, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Aggregated mean slope at ecoregion scale. Affects stream power, flow velocity, and sediment dynamics.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level II ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Zonal skewness NED slope values, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Measures asymmetry in slope distribution. Helps identify dominant terrain types and slope transitions.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level II ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Zonal standard deviation (SD) of slope values from NED data, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Quantifies slope variability including extremes. Suggests rugged or heterogeneous terrain.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level II ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Zonal interquartile range (IQR) of NED slope values, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Measures slope variability using IQR. Robust to outliers; reflects terrain complexity and infiltration dynamics.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level II ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Zonal modal fraction of surface soil from zero to 5 cm composed of clay particles from SSURGO2, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Indicates surface soil texture. Higher clay content reduces infiltration and increases runoff potential.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level II ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Zonal modal fraction of surface soil from zero to 5 cm composed of silt particles from SSURGO2, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Indicates intermediate soil texture. Balances water retention and infiltration capacity.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level II ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Zonal modal fraction of surface soil from zero to 5 cm composed of sand particles from SSURGO2, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Represents infiltration rate of surface soils. Low values indicate higher runoff and steeper hydrographs.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level II ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Zonal median of Strahler stream order, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Represents typical drainage network complexity. Based on Strahler order, indicating average stream hierarchy within the watershed.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level II ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Zonal maximum stream order in the network, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Indicates the largest stream order within the catchment. Useful for identifying drainage basin scale and extent.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level II ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Standard deviation of seasonal precip totals from PRISM 1991 to 2020 normals aggegated to Level III ecoregions.
Notes: Captures variability across seasons. Sensitive to outliers—useful for detecting flashiness or hydrologic irregularity.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level III ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: IQR (25th to 75th percentile) of seasonal precip totals from PRISM 1991 to 2020 normals aggegated to Level III ecoregions.
Notes: Characterizes intra-annual precipitation variability; robust to outliers.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level III ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Sum of zonal medians of fall monthly precip totals (Sep to Nov) from PRISM 1991 to 2020 normals aggegated to Level III ecoregions.
Notes: Captures fall precipitation; relevant to baseflow reset and transition to frontal storm systems.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level III ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Sum of zonal medians of winter monthly precip (Dec to Feb) from PRISM 1991 to 2020 normals aggegated to Level III ecoregions.
Notes: Indicates snowpack formation potential and winter water storage.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level III ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Sum of zonal medians of summer monthly precip (Jun to Aug) from PRISM 1991 to 2020 normals aggegated to Level III ecoregions.
Notes: Key springtime recharge and flood generation season; relevant to melt-transition systems and early crop needs.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level III ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Sum of zonal medians of spring monthly precip (Mar to May) from PRISM 1990 to 2020 normals aggegated to Level III ecoregions.
Notes: Captures convective storm seasonality (flood-prone regions).
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level III ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Zonal median of percent cover of dominant land class (cropland, forest, etc.) from MODIS 2016 land cover, aggegated to Level III ecoregions.
Notes: Summarizes dominant land cover class by proportion within a zone. Helps interpret complex or fragmented landscapes by reducing pixel-level detail to a single representative class.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level III ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Normalized Shannon-Weiner Diversity Index of MODIS land classes aggegated to Level III ecoregions.
Notes: Reflects land use heterogeneity. Higher values indicate fragmented or mixed land cover, which may affect infiltration and runoff patterns.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level III ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Zonal median of surface roughness, derived from 10 m NED, aggegated to Level III ecoregions.
Notes: Captures fine-scale surface texture. Influences ponding, microrelief, and infiltration pathways.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level III ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Categorical version of the Topographic Wetness Index (TWI), created by binning continuous TWI values into ordinal classes (e.g., quartiles or hydrologically relevant thresholds). Simplifies terrain and moisture interactions for modeling and interpretability.
Notes: Indicates average terrain wetness potential. Combines slope and upstream drainage area.  Lower classes indicate drier conditions; higher classes represent wetter zones with greater runoff accumulation potential.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level III ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Zonal mode of 10 m NED Topographic Wetness Index (TWI) values aggegated to Level III ecoregions.
Notes: Shows most frequent wetness class. Useful for identifying dominant moisture or runoff conditions.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level III ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Zonal assignment  of ordinal NED Topographic Wetness Index (TWI) classes, derived from 10 m NED, aggegated to Level III ecoregions.
Notes: Ordinal wetness class derived from TWI. Simplifies terrain–moisture interactions; lower values = drier, higher = wetter zones.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level III ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Zonal median of STATSGO2 permeability values aggegated to Level III ecoregions.
Notes: Represents infiltration rate of surface soils. Low values indicate higher runoff and steeper hydrographs.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level III ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Zonal modal soil hydrologic group (A to D) from STATSGO2 aggegated to Level III ecoregions.
Notes: USDA hydrologic soil group (A to D). Classifies soils by infiltration capacity and storm response.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level III ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Zonal median of 10 m NED flow accumulation (upslope contributing area) aggegated to Level III ecoregions.
Notes: Estimates upslope contributing area. Higher values suggest greater potential for water accumulation and flooding.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000 to 100,000 sq-km, based on Level III ecoregion size and heterogeneity

Description: Zonal count of freeze–thaw transition days from PRISM daily data (1991 to 2020), aggegated to NHD+ catchments.
Notes: Captures thermally transitional zones; relevant for soil structure, infiltration disruption, and freeze thaw runoff events.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1 to 5 sq-km (catchment scale, NHD+)

Description: Zonal median of 95th percentile of daily precip on wet days from PRISM daily normals (1991 to 2020), aggegated to NHD+ catchments.
Notes: Captures storm severity at the upper tail. Correlated with flash flood potential and runoff generation efficiency.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1 to 5 sq-km (catchment scale, NHD+)

Description: Zonal median number of wet days (less than 0.1 mm/day) per season from PRISM daily normals (1991 to 2020), aggregated to NHD+ catchments.
Notes: Describes storm frequency and seasonal spacing. Interacts with intensity to shape hydrograph form and flood likelihood.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1 to 5 sq-km (catchment scale, NHD+)

Description: Zonal median percent cover by dominant NLCD class aggegated to NHD+ catchments.
Notes: Shows dominant land cover proportion at the catchment scale. Useful for linking terrain features with hydrologic behavior.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1 to 5 sq-km (catchment scale, NHD+)

Description: Normalized Shannon Weiner Diversity Index of NLCD land cover classes, aggregated to NHD+ catchments.
Notes: Measures land cover diversity within a catchment. Supports modeling of transitions or mosaic land use patterns.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1 to 5 sq-km (catchment scale, NHD+)

Description: Zonal median elevation range (max minus min elevation) from 10 m NED data, aggregated to NHD+ catchments.
Notes: Captures elevation spread within catchment. Linked to slope energy, erosion risk, and runoff response.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1 to 5 sq-km (catchment scale, NHD+)

Description: Zonal median of the cosine of aspect, derived from 10 m NED data, aggregated to NHD+ catchments.
Notes: Quantifies N to S slope orientation. North-facing slopes (values > 0) retain snow longer and reduce evapotranspiration.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1 to 5 sq-km (catchment scale, NHD+)

Description: Zonal median of the sine of aspect, derived from 10 m NED data, aggregated to NHD+ catchments.
Notes: Quantifies E to W slope orientation. East-facing slopes (values > 0) warm earlier, affecting snowmelt and phenology.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1 to 5 sq-km (catchment scale, NHD+)

Description: IQR of combined curvature types, derived from 10 m NED data, aggregated to NHD+ catchments.
Notes: Measures variation in terrain curvature. High values imply complex flow paths and erosion susceptibility.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1 to 5 sq-km (catchment scale, NHD+)

Description: Zonal median of planform (horizontal) curvature, derived from 10 m NED data, aggregated to NHD+ catchments.
Notes: Identifies slope convergence/divergence. Negative = concave (channels), positive = convex (ridges).
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1 to 5 sq-km (catchment scale, NHD+)

Description: Zonal median of profile (vertical) curvature, derived from 10 m NED data, aggregated to NHD+ catchments.
Notes: Represents slope change along flow lines. Helps distinguish depositional vs. erosional terrain zones.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1 to 5 sq-km (catchment scale, NHD+)

Description: Watershed elongation ratio, calculated from catchment geometry, aggregated to NHD+ catchments.
Notes: Describes catchment shape. More elongated basins have faster runoff and flashier peaks.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1 to 5 sq-km (catchment scale, NHD+)

Description: Watershed circularity ratio, calculated from catchment geometry, aggregated to NHD+ catchments.
Notes: Captures catchment compactness. Higher values suggest faster, more concentrated runoff response.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1 to 5 sq-km (catchment scale, NHD+)

Description: Zonal median of stream length per catchment area, derived from NHD+ data.
Notes: Ratio of total stream length to catchment area. Higher density reflects greater drainage dissection and shorter runoff travel times.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1 to 5 sq-km (catchment scale, NHD+)

Description: Zonal median of average flow path length, derived from NHD+ data.
Notes: Average flow path length to outlet. Longer paths typically indicate delayed runoff response.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1 to 5 sq-km (catchment scale, NHD+)

Description: Zonal median of stream slope (elevation drop per unit flow length), derived from NHD+ data.
Notes: Elevation drop per unit stream length. Influences runoff velocity and hydrograph shape.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1 to 5 sq-km (catchment scale, NHD+)

Description: Relief ratio (elevation range divided by stream length) from 10 m NED data, aggregated to NHD+ catchments.
Notes: Ratio of watershed relief to main channel length. High values indicate steep basins and higher hydrologic energy.
Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1 to 5 sq-km (catchment scale, NHD+)
